title: Naval Ravikant on decisions, long-term thinking, and founders: The Knowledge Project
summary: Naval explains how he approaches decisions (leverage, mental models, systems over goals), why compounding only works with long-term people, and what he looks for in founders and counterparties. Much of the interview covers reading, happiness and education, which is not business-relevant. The business and decision-making material is the durable part.

principles.text: Judgment is leveraged: small gains in decision accuracy are worth far more when capital and teams multiply them.
principles.quote: someone who makes decisions right 80% of the time instead of 70% of the time will be valued and compensated in the market hundreds of times more.

principles.text: Success is mostly about avoiding mistakes; eliminate what won't work rather than predicting what will.
principles.quote: I think being successful is just about not making mistakes. It’s not about having correct judgment. It’s about avoiding the incorrect judgments.

principles.text: Build a system with wide sampling and the option to double down, rather than relying on individual picks.
principles.quote: my system is I want to see 10,000 companies and I want to pick 500 that have a shot of being huge. Then I want the option to double down on the five winners.

principles.text: Benefits come from compounding, so work only with long-term people on long-term payoffs.
principles.quote: I think all the benefits in life come from compound interest, whether in money or in relationships or love or health or activities or habits.

principles.text: Ideas are commodities; the combination of idea, execution and passion is what wins.
principles.quote: It’s about the combination of the idea plus the execution plus the passion.

principles.text: High-integrity counterparties make deals easy and durable; unhappy deals unwind and never compound.
principles.quote: Negotiations with high-integrity people are usually very easy. You’re giving each other things to make sure the other person is happy enough that the deal survives.
